$comment: The edge modules were the only TypeScript in this repo nobody typechecked.
Vitest transforms them with esbuild, which strips types without checking them, so
`pnpm test` went green on code that `tsc` would have rejected — and it is the code
that verifies signatures and decides who has paid. `strict`,
`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` were on for every other
package and off, silently, for this one.
The entrypoints are excluded rather than fixed: `_src/*/index.ts` is Deno source. It
imports with `.ts` specifiers and calls `Deno.serve`, neither of which is valid under
this compiler, and adding Deno's types to a Node project to typecheck two files would
trade a real check for a fake one. What is checked here is everything the entrypoints
delegate to, which is where the decisions live.
